prompt: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun, yet Venus is hotter at its surface. Why?

options.text: Venus spins much faster, generating friction heat
Venus is covered in active volcanoes that heat the whole surface
Venus has a very thick carbon dioxide atmosphere that traps heat
Venus has a molten surface facing the Sun at all times

explanation: Venus's thick carbon dioxide atmosphere creates a runaway greenhouse effect, trapping heat so the surface reaches about 465°C — hotter than Mercury's.
